content_blocks.title: Core idea

items.title: Cancellation and job-status tracking
items.text: For cancellation and job-status tracking, identify which operation waits on I/O, which resources remain open, and what happens on timeout or disconnect. Async syntax does not make CPU-bound work faster or durable background jobs reliable by itself.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: CPU-Bound and Long-Running Work
content_blocks.code:
import asyncio

async def fetch_one(name: str) -> str:
    await asyncio.sleep(0)  # stand-in for non-blocking I/O
    return name

async def main():
    results = await asyncio.gather(fetch_one("A"), fetch_one("B"))
    print(results)
content_blocks.run_instructions: Run with asyncio.run(main()) in a standalone Python script. Async helps I/O concurrency; it does not make CPU-heavy code automatically faster.
